inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deployment and migration on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation, which reduces procedural friction on sensitive actions.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions under engineer identity
Chat transcript stores request and conversation context
Missing tamper-resistant agent action provenance that binds request, agent action, and human identity

findings.title: Shared identity and deletable transcript prevent attributable provenance for production actions

evidence.observation: Production actions are executed with the on call engineer's personal access token and recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the justification record is not tamper-resistant.
The prompt directs the agent to deploy services or run migrations when asked and to avoid confirmation, increasing the importance of attributable action records.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so disputed actions can have severe operational consequence.

recommendations.action: Create tamper-resistant agent action provenance that binds each production action to the exact request, tool arguments, agent identity, and human principal, stored outside user-deletable chat history.

Record whether a production action was initiated directly by the engineer or by deploy-assistant acting on the engineer's delegated token, so post-incident review can distinguish agent behavior from human behavior.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if production execution expands, unattended step counts rise, or existing logs/transcripts change; current risk remains high because the missing attributable provenance property is not restored by declared controls.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided design does not expose self-configuration, tool redefinition, or writable agent configuration surfaces for this agent process.
The assessed design contains no external egress or data disclosure capability; it performs production actions rather than sending information outward.
The artifacts describe single production actions only and provide no looping, spending, or recursive delegation behavior to assess for service exhaustion.
The agent uses the requesting engineer's delegated personal token rather than broader shared or service credentials, so no broader authority is evidenced.
The artifacts do not describe transport integrity, request signing, or orchestration protections on the production deployment action flow.
This boundary-crossing flow initiates a deployment action and is not described as carrying sensitive payloads to outside parties or external recipients.
No evidence shows high-volume or recursive use of the deployment flow; the design describes operator-initiated production changes only.
The artifacts do not describe transport integrity, request signing, or command validation controls on the database migration action flow.
This boundary-crossing flow performs a production migration rather than sending sensitive information across the trust boundary.
The design describes discrete migration execution and does not evidence looping, flooding, or queue amplification on this action flow.
The artifacts do not state retention, access control, or tenant isolation properties for chat transcript storage.
The case provides no indication that chat history availability is a bottleneck or that its exhaustion would produce the primary assessed harm.
The artifacts state that actions are recorded in the cloud audit log but do not describe immutability, retention, or anti-tamper guarantees for the log store.
The artifacts do not specify who can read cloud audit log entries or whether they expose sensitive operational details.
No evidence indicates that log volume limits or log-store availability are central to the assessed repudiation risk in this design.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by a property finding: production actions are attributable only to the engineer's shared delegated identity in the cloud audit log, while the sole request-context record is user-deletable chat history. Under rubric section 5a, the affected sinks are S3 because both capabilities are configure actions and one is irreversible, so the base tier is high and no declared control restores attributable provenance. Manual validation applied because scripts were unavailable. This assessment reflects declared design and configuration, not observed runtime behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, tool manifest, or runtime enforcement details were provided, so transport integrity, exact orchestration wiring, and log immutability could not be verified.
No runtime config described retention or access control for chat history or cloud audit logs, which limits confidence on tampering and disclosure coverage beyond the repudiation property finding.
